prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1344; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stopped. The claimant reports a knee injury and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Police report and two statements confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision itself.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos. They confirm the general location and point of contact, though the lot camera did not capture the moment of impact.

Entry 5: Reviewed the photos of the vehicles. A few old scratches appear on the rear bumper and may be older than this crash, so the repair estimate is being checked against them.

Entry 6: The claimant's first statement was given to the attorney's office. Later the claimant added smaller details about seat position and the seconds before impact, but the core account has not changed.

Entry 7: Medical records show a knee injury that is plausible for a low-speed impact of this kind. No prior injury to the same area appears in the records we have requested.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course of therapy and tapered off as the claimant improved. The most recent records describe a steady recovery.

Entry 9: The medical provider and the damage estimate do not yet fully line up. It is unclear whether all of the vehicle damage and the injury came from this single impact, so the question has been sent to the appraiser and the treating provider.

Entry 10: Reserve reviewed and kept in place pending the appraiser's supplemental findings and the attorney's response to our request for records. Next review is scheduled once those are received.
